name: Proto-North Sarawak
orthography_note: Blust writes PNS schwa ə where PMP has *e (2007: 6-7), and the voiced aspirates bʰ dʰ jʰ gʰ.
notes: Kelabitic, Kenyah, Berawan-Lower Baram and Bintulu (Blust 2007: 7, Table 3; 2002: 384). Its defining innovation is the split of the PMP voiced obstruents into plain voiced stops and voiced aspirates (Blust 2007: 7). Entered under PMP from Blust's Table 2, although decision smith-higher-order holds Smith's North Sarawak back (decision pns-node). Glottolog's North Sarawakan (nort3171) has the same members.
inherit_note: Unchanged: Table 2 (Blust 2007: 6) gives the same symbol for PNS.

name: Proto-Kenyah
notes: Highland and Lowland Kenyah, the latter including Sebop and Penan (Blust 2007: 6, Figure 1). PK kept the PNS voiced aspirates as a distinct series (p. 7) and had a six-vowel system, adding *e and *o by lowering before final *h from *R and *s (p. 10). Glottolog's Kenyahic (keny1280) has Kenyah, Sebop and Penan.
inherit_note: Not among the changes that 'distinguish Proto-Kenyah from PNS' (Blust 2007: 7): retained.

name: Chamorro
orthography_note: Topping's spelling as Blust (2000: 84-85) uses it: ' glottal stop, ch [ts], y [dz] (Blust respells final -ai, -ao, -ui as -ay, -aw, -uy), ñ, ng, gw. Low front æ is not written in the dictionary; Blust marks it as ([æ]).
notes: Mariana Islands. Blust (2000) states its reflexes against PMP (p. 88) and finds no subgroup between the two: Chamorro is a primary branch of Malayo-Polynesian with no close relatives (§4, pp. 103-104). Glottocode from Glottolog 5.4.

name: Palauan
orthography_note: Blust's phonemicization (2009: 308): y and w are glides, written i/e and u/o in the standard orthography; ð is written d, ʔ ch, ŋ ng.
notes: Palau. With Chamorro one of the two non-Oceanic Austronesian languages of the Pacific (Blust 2000: 83); Blust (2009) states its reflexes against PMP (Table 2, p. 309) and gives it no closer relatives. Glottocode from Glottolog 5.4.

name: Òma Lóngh
orthography_note: Soriente's spelling (Blust 2007: 8-9): é è ó ò are tense and lax mid vowels, e is both [ə] and [ɯ] (from *u), j is [ɟ] (unreleased [c] finally), f [ɸ], v [β], gh [ɣ], ngh a voiceless velar nasal. Blust writes ʔ for Soriente's apostrophe.
notes: Upper Malinau and upper Pujungan rivers, East Kalimantan; about 3,000 speakers, long isolated from other Kenyah (Blust 2007: 8). A Highland Kenyah language (p. 10); Blust derives it from Proto-Kenyah. Data from Soriente (2006). Glottolog 5.4: Uma' Lung, under Highland Kenyah (Upper Pujungan).

name: Kiput
orthography_note: Blust's spelling (2002: 385): e is schwa, é a mid front vowel, ë a mid-central glide in falling diphthongs, c a voiceless palatal affricate, ʔ the glottal stop; I and U are lax vowels of loanwords. Final -ey, -ew are written -ei-, -eu- before a final consonant.
notes: One longhouse (Long Kiput) on the Baram River, Sarawak; about 450 speakers. Berawan-Lower Baram branch of North Sarawak (Blust 2002: 384). Blust derives it directly from PNS (p. 385); Lower Baram and Berawan-Lower Baram nodes are not entered. Glottocode from Glottolog 5.4 (North Sarawakan > Berawan-Lower Baram > Lower Baram > Central Lower Baram A).
inherit_note: Unchanged: 'It will be assumed that no change has taken place unless stated otherwise' (Blust 2002: 423), in the summary of shifts, splits and mergers.
